reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read "daughter of Omri" as granddaughter — Athaliah was Ahab's daughter and Omri's granddaughter, so the two titles describe one woman.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells of the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, the source page for this entry, presses that the texts name two different fathers — Omri in 2 Kings 8:26 and 2 Chronicles 22:2, Ahab in 2 Kings 8:18 and 2 Chronicles 21:6 — and that one man cannot be both.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: Skeptic's Annotated Bible ("Who was Athaliah's father?")

excerpts.excerpt_text: Athaliah the daughter of Omri—more properly, "granddaughter." The expression is used loosely, as the statement was made simply for the purpose of intimating that she belonged to that idolatrous race.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the Omri/Ahab wording: 'daughter of Omri' = granddaughter, used loosely; this is the core harmonization of the named tension.

excerpts.excerpt_text: In Kg2 8:26 and Ch2 22:2 she is called the daughter, i.e., grand-daughter, of Omri; for, according to Kg2 8:18, she was a daughter of Ahab. Omri, the grand-father, is mentioned in Kg2 8:26 as the founder of the dynasty which brought so much trouble upon Israel and Judah through its idolatry.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Names all the conflicting verses (8:26, 22:2 'of Omri'; 8:18 'of Ahab') and resolves: daughter of Ahab, granddaughter of Omri the dynasty-founder.

excerpts.excerpt_text: She was Ahab's daughter, who was the son of Omri.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Compact cross-ID stating the generational chain Athaliah—Ahab—Omri, exactly the relationship the contradiction turns on.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-75), on 2 Kings 8:25
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: Treats this passage directly: names 2 Kgs 8:26 / 2 Chr 22:2 ('of Omri') against 2 Kgs 8:18 ('of Ahab') and resolves the wording as daughter of Ahab, granddaughter of Omri the dynasty-founder.
